lane_impact: L-combat-core (§4 blocker ④ 'multi-target per-hit rule (full vs falloff)' closed and the §1 unknown-unknown deleted), L-ui-hud (combo semantics = distinct enemies). Note the neutralList is swept by the same loop, so civilians/animals are cuttable by a stray arc.
ledger_text: **Multi-target damage rule** (one arc hits N enemies — full damage each? falloff toward the tip?).
text: One arc hitting N enemies deals the same full Damage object to every one of them — no falloff toward the tip and no split — each enemy hit at most once per slash (gotHitFlag), broad-phased by a ±200 px horizontal window, and the combo counter increments by the number of DISTINCT enemies hit, not by hits.

lane_impact: L-combat-core, L-enemies-ai, L-items-equipment (weak points are literally paperdoll slots, so the weak-point table and the equipment layer table are the same table).
ledger_text: **Hit-registration window** (instant at release vs an active sweep an enemy can dodge into/out of).
text: Hit registration is instantaneous at slash resolution, evaluated by walking the released polyline point-by-point — there is no swept active window an enemy can dodge into or out of — and resolution walks the paperdoll part list FRONT-to-BACK so the topmost part struck decides the hit (which is the actual mechanism behind 'shielder legs / undead heads' weak points).

lane_impact: L-economy (blocker ② half-closed) and L-items-equipment (blocker ③ closed). The ledger's own observation is reproduced exactly by the true mechanism: 5c = a light item with 0 modifiers (1+0)x5; 25c = the same item with 4 modifiers (1+4)x5. The mechanism is affix count x weight class, not rarity/level.
ledger_text: **Sell price is NOT flat per item** — it scales with rarity/level (same sword 5c and 25c). Don't encode flat-per-type.
text: Sell price is (1 + affixModifierCount) x 10 for items of weight >= 10 and x 5 below that, with anything itemID < 3000 selling for a flat 1 — it does NOT scale with rarity or level, and it is identical in both builds.

ledger_text: ④ SPD→cooldown formula.
text: The SPEED→cooldown transfer function is linear and hard-capped: cooldowns are multiplied by 1 − min(SPD,300)/300 × 0.5, so SPEED 300 is the cap and buys exactly a 50% cooldown reduction; the SPEED buff multiplies SPD by 1.5 before the clamp.
